title: The AI Daily — Morning Conversation
blurb: An American-English dialogue limited to publisher feed excerpts.
lines: Hey, welcome to The AI Daily. I'm Maya, and Ben is here with me. We've picked a few headlines from publisher news feeds to talk through.
Hi, Maya. These are short feed excerpts, not the full articles, so we'll keep the facts carefully attributed and avoid filling in the blanks.
Let's start with The Decoder. The headline is: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model.
According to the publisher's excerpt, Bytedance and several US universities introduce Axion 1.0, an AI agent that rivals top commercial models from OpenAI and Anthropic…
That brings us to Crunchbase News, which has this headline: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: $400M For Neurotech Leads, Followed By Big Deals For AI, Fintech, Biotech And More.
According to the publisher's excerpt, U.S. startups continued to secure sizable rounds, led by brain-computer interface company Science securing a fresh $400 million.
Next up, Google News · Anthropic reports: Anthropic mathematician says he used AI to solve the Riemann hypothesis - Business Insider.
According to the publisher's excerpt, Anthropic mathematician says he used AI to solve the Riemann hypothesis Business Insider
And our fourth story is from TechCrunch Startups: Experts warn: Nearly everyone in AI is susceptible to a honey-trap scheme right now.
According to the publisher's excerpt, Techies are building technology that can advance all aspects of the world — but can they protect their hearts? That's…
Before we go, here's a useful expression: keep an eye on. It means watch something for changes — like a fast-moving AI story.
Exactly. And look into means investigate further. Follow the original reporting for context. See you in the next edition.
note: AI voices reading a conservative two-host script grounded only in publisher feed excerpts. Full article claims were not independently verified.
